Proposed next steps (can we align on these by end of week?):
- You confirm procurement path (PO vs card vs marketplace) and the legal/finance contact for vendor paperwork.
- I attach the demo recording and a short cost comparison (hosted vs dedicated) — Marcus will flag options tuned to your latency and retention needs.
- If PO is required, we can prepare a vendor packet + standard SOW template; if card/marketplace, then we can do a short POC and convert to a commit after usage validation.

Hi Laura — appreciate the summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- Payment path: Procurement will prefer a PO. We rarely use corporate card at enterprise scale. We *can* buy via AWS Marketplace but only for certain vendors where procurement has a marketplace buying playbook. Can you confirm if Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace and whether purchase there supports committed pricing?
- Hosting: Security prefers Dedicated for anything with PHI or user PII. For this initial pilot (anonymized test data) we could start on Hosted to move quickly and then plan to migrate to Dedicated for production.

Action items for us: procurement will send a standard vendor questionnaire (we attach it to this thread). Legal will want an IL/DP addendum if we move to Dedicated with customer-controlled keys. Tom (CFO) will need the committed vs on-demand cost delta for budgeting.

Can you send a vendor packet and an estimate split (hosted-on-demand vs dedicated 3-month commit vs dedicated 12-month commit)? Also confirm marketplace status.

Thanks — happy to do the call tomorrow 10–10:30 PT if that works for you.

Thanks — drafting the numbers now. Key points for quote: 
- Hosted (on-demand): per-token pricing with no commit; good for pilot, low ops friction.
- Dedicated reserved (3mo): 20% discount over on-demand, predictable throughput, recommended if steady peak traffic > 3M tokens/day.
- Dedicated reserved (12mo): 35% discount + optional burst credit; includes SLA credit and preferred routing.

Marketplace note: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace but committed pricing requires a SaaS contract outside the marketplace UI for multi-month reserved capacity. That said, we can accept initial purchase via marketplace for up to 90 days of consumption and then transition to a reserved contract for the commitment — procurement will need to sign a reserved capacity addendum. I'll attach a draft estimate and a short note on the transition flows.

Attaching: draft_estimate_hosting_vs_dedicated.xlsx (will update with numerics).

— Marcus

Hi Samantha / team — attaching the vendor packet and a conservative cost comparison as requested. Highlights below to share with Tom and procurement: 

- Marketplace: Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace for standard SaaS purchases. Committed reserved pricing (dedicated pools) requires a reserved capacity addendum and a direct contract, but we can start with a marketplace purchase for the pilot and transition to a reserved contract without service interruption.
- Pricing snapshot (high level): Hosted on-demand = lower up-front, variable monthly; Dedicated 3-month commit = ~20% lower than hosted (applies when stable throughput is expected); Dedicated 12-month commit = ~35% lower + SLA credits. Full breakdown in attached spreadsheet.
- Legal/compliance: we'll provide an IL/DP addendum for Dedicated deployments; engineering can provide architecture and key-management notes for your security review.

Attachments included: Novus_vendor_questionnaire_filled.pdf (completed vendor questionnaire), draft_estimate_hosting_vs_dedicated.xlsx (costs), demo_recording_20260315.mp4 (short demo).

Proposed commercial path (based on your signals):
1) Pilot on Hosted (marketplace or card) for 4–6 weeks to validate accuracy and performance.
2) Procurement signs PO for 3-month Dedicated reserve if pilot meets KPIs; we lock price via a reserved capacity addendum.
3) Post-PO: optional conversion to 12-month commit with retroactive credits if you want deeper discounts and longer-term SLA.

Can your procurement team complete the attached vendor questionnaire and confirm the PO contact (name + email)? If it helps, I can join your procurement call tomorrow at 10 PT to walk the packet.
